subject: Biotechnology
title: Bioinformatics Revolution
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bioinformatics Revolution usable.

hook.text: Genomics generates more data than astronomy — bioinformatics is the computational backbone that makes biology data-driven.

buildup.text: Sequence alignment, genome assembly, and protein structure prediction — algorithms turn raw data into biological understanding.

discovery.text: Cloud computing gives any researcher access to petabyte-scale genomic datasets — democratizing data analysis globally.

twist.text: Data generation outpaces analysis — most genomic data is stored but never analyzed, creating a growing interpretation bottleneck.

climax.text: Foundation models trained on protein and DNA sequences generalize across tasks — one model for structure, function, and design.

punchline.text: Biology becomes an information science — bioinformatics turns sequences into solutions.

quiz.question: What is the growing bottleneck in genomics?
options: Sequencing technology has reached its accuracy limits
Data generation far outpaces analysis, so most genomic data is stored but never interpreted
There are not enough genomes left to sequence
